title: Sense-specific Historical Word Usage Generation

selection.evidence: Cited by saponara2026 [14] and cassotti2025 [15]: Janus generated the SemEval-2027 Task 3 synthetic dev data and is the organisers' prototype generator for Subtask 2; its WSD model is on HF as ChangeIsKey/graded-wsd.

cost.compute_notes: TACL PDF pp. 1-11 read in full (main body); appendices skimmed. Models (ChangeIsKey/llama3-janus, graded-wsd, text-dating) not run.

triggers: generate example sentences for a sense definition and year
graded WSD model usage definition relatedness OED
do LLM generated usages repeat themselves
annotator agreement lower for older texts

claims.statement: Llama 3 8B fine-tuned (QLoRA) on 1.19M OED example sentences, input 'year <|t|> word <|t|> definition <|s|>', generates usages that are as temporally accurate as real OED examples (decade-classifier RMSE 54.75 vs 52.75 years; instructed GPT-4o/Llama 108-148) and more varied than instructed LLMs (pairwise SBERT cosine 0.35 vs 0.47-0.59).
claims.scope: OED test lemmas (2,768, disjoint from training); one sampled year per (word, sense); English only.

our_assessment.why: Temporal accuracy is measured by a decade classifier whose own RMSE on real text is ~48-53 years, so 'as accurate as OED' means 'as hard to date as OED for this classifier'. Variability is the more practical finding: instructed LLMs repeat themselves, which matters for any prototype built from generated usages (arena-lsc llm_proto.py uses an instructed model).

claims.statement: A roberta-large usage-definition classifier trained on OED relations (Exact/Peer/Related/Homograph) reaches Spearman 0.76 and Exact-vs-Different macro-F1 0.83 on real OED test usages; generated usages score 0.59-0.64 / 0.74-0.77. Human (MTurk, 3 per pair) vs OED labels: 0.57-0.58 Spearman, F1 0.72, the same for Janus and OED usages.
claims.scope: Tables 5 and 7; the classifier is released as ChangeIsKey/graded-wsd (English).

our_assessment.why: Reported clearly, and the human F1 of 0.72 against OED labels is a useful ceiling: OED's own peer/related distinctions are noisy (the authors say so), so a binary 'is it this sense' task over dictionary definitions has a human ceiling well below 1 - consistent with the 0.86 annotator-vs-annotator F1 measured on DWUG DE Sense in arena-lsc.

claims.statement: Human semantic-accuracy agreement (Spearman with OED labels) rises with the text's date, from about 0.45 for the earliest 50-year bins to over 0.7 for modern ones; the same trend holds for the WSD model.
claims.scope: Figures 4-5; small samples per early bin.

our_assessment.why: Read from figures, not tables (no exact values); direction is clear and plausible. Relevant to SemEval-2027 Task 3, whose periods start in 1880: older usages are harder for humans and models alike, so per-period error analysis should expect worse early periods.

checked.how: HF API listing and graded-wsd model card read
checked.result: present; not run (English-only; Janus 8B fp16 does not fit next to other models on a 12 GB GPU without quantisation)

relations.why: Same authors; that paper uses Janus for prototypes.

open_questions: Does graded-wsd (English) beat a local instruction LLM judge on Subtask 2 for English? Needs an English sense-annotated set with definitions; none in the arena-lsc pool.
